sonnet.q1: The gateway returns 401 Unauthorized. No counter is read or written.
sonnet.q2: All of a customer's keys share one budget, so in total 100 requests per minute on a Standard plan (Enterprise limit is not decided).
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (it may also carry X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0). The backend never sees the request; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. A rejected request is not counted and uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. Counted requests use budget even if the backend fails; the 5xx is passed on unchanged and the count stays.
sonnet.q6: The gateway fails open: it forwards the request to the backend anyway, emits the metric ratelimit_store_unavailable, and sends no X-RateLimit headers. The count may be off by one.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: no limit decided yet (open); the proposed v1 placeholder skips the check, with no counter and no headers, pending Product's confirmation.
sonnet.q8: In a shared Redis counter under the key rl:<customerId>, shared by all six gateway instances. Old counts are removed by Redis key expiry: the key is set to expire after 60 seconds on the first count.
sonnet.q9: When the 60-second window ends. The Redis key expires 60 seconds after the customer's first counted request, which resets the count to zero (the next counted request starts a new window).
sonnet.q10: The check and count is done as one Redis script that Redis runs as a single unit (atomic), so two instances cannot both pass when only one slot is left.
sonnet.q11: From the time left in the window (ttl_ms) returned by Redis: ceil(ttl_ms / 1000) seconds, with a minimum of 1. The gateway's clock does not matter.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether the gateway retries the store (the document describes only forwarding the request with no retry mentioned). The client gets no X-RateLimit headers, just the backend response.
